# Therapy Session: Marcus Webb, 34

## Client Background

**Marcus Webb** is a 34-year-old former high school history teacher from Cleveland, Ohio. He was once considered one of the most passionate and beloved teachers at his school, winning a district award for excellence in education three years in a row. He left teaching two years ago after a painful and public divorce from his wife of seven years, **Dana**, who had an affair with one of Marcus's close colleagues, **Ryan**. The betrayal devastated him professionally and personally, as he and Ryan had coached the school's debate team together for four years.

Marcus now works a remote data entry job that he describes as "soul-crushing." He lives alone in a small apartment in a Cleveland suburb, has gained roughly 40 pounds since the divorce, and has largely withdrawn from his social circle. He has a nine-year-old daughter, **Lily**, who lives with Dana and visits Marcus every other weekend. He grew up with a emotionally distant and highly critical father, **Gerald**, and carries deep-seated beliefs about being fundamentally unworthy of love. He has been seeing Dr. Patricia Okafor for about eight weeks.

---

## 100 Client Statements

---

1. "I don't even know where to start today, Dr. Okafor. I just feel like everything is gray."

2. "I woke up at 3 a.m. again on Tuesday, and I just lay there staring at the water stain on my bedroom ceiling for two hours."

3. "The data entry job — I sit there clicking the same fields over and over, and I genuinely cannot tell you what I do anymore. I've stopped caring."

4. "I used to plan entire units on the Civil Rights Movement. I used to get excited about that. I can't even imagine feeling excited about anything now."

5. "Lily called me on Thursday and she was telling me about her soccer game, and I could hear myself giving these flat, hollow responses, and I hated myself for it."

6. "I don't want her to grow up and remember her dad as the sad guy in the dim apartment."

7. "Sometimes I think me leaving teaching was the last real decision I was capable of making, and even that one was terrible."

8. "I stepped on the scale this morning and I just turned the bathroom light off and walked away. I couldn't even deal with the number."

9. "My dad used to say 'pull yourself together' like it was the simplest thing in the world, and lately his voice is just constantly in my head."

10. "I know intellectually that Dana and Ryan getting together wasn't entirely my fault, but I still feel like I must have done something fundamentally wrong."

11. "There's a part of me that goes through everything — every argument, every trip we took, every dinner — looking for the moment I lost her, and I can't stop doing it."

12. "Ryan was in my wedding. He stood up there in a gray suit and shook my hand. I still can't process that."

13. "I've been avoiding the whole east side of Cleveland because that's where the school is and I'm terrified I'll run into someone who knows me."

14. "My friend Derek texted me three times this week and I just couldn't bring myself to respond. I don't know what I'd even say."

15. "I rehearse conversations in my head before I make any phone call, even just to order food, and if it doesn't go the way I planned I spiral."

16. "I went to the grocery store on Saturday and there was a couple laughing by the bread aisle and I had to leave. I just abandoned my cart and left."

17. "I know that sounds ridiculous. I know it does."

18. "There's this specific feeling I get around Sunday evenings — like a physical weight on my chest — and it starts around 4 p.m. and doesn't lift until I fall asleep."

19. "I've been sleeping about eleven hours and still feeling exhausted. What does that even mean?"

20. "I don't think I'm a danger to myself, I want to be clear about that. But I have been thinking more about just... not existing for a while. Like pressing pause."

21. "Not death. Just — a break from being me. Is that a thing?"

22. "My apartment has this smell now. Like stale takeout and recycled air. And I've just gotten used to it, which is somehow worse."

23. "I ordered Chinese food four times last week from the same place and the delivery guy recognized me and gave me this look and it humiliated me."

24. "I keep all the blinds down. I told myself it was because of the neighbor's porch light, but that's not really why."

25. "When Lily visits, I clean everything, I open the windows, I buy fresh fruit — and then she leaves and within 48 hours the place goes back to what it is."

26. "That's not healthy, right? That she's the only thing that can make me function like a normal person?"

27. "I've been having these moments at work — just sitting at my keyboard — where I realize ten minutes have passed and I don't know where they went."

28. "My body feels heavy all the time. Like I'm wearing a wet coat indoors and I can't take it off."

29. "I used to run. I used to do a 5K every spring. My running shoes are still by the door and every morning I look at them and go make coffee instead."

30. "I think about my students sometimes. Marcus Holloway — this kid who used to argue with me about everything — I wonder if he's okay. I wonder if I let him down by leaving."

31. "I believe that people don't really change, and I hate that I believe that, because it means I've been like this my whole life under the surface."

32. "My dad never told me he loved me. Not once that I can actually remember. And I used to be okay with that, but lately it's been eating at me."

33. "I have a very clear memory of showing him a history paper I got an A on in seventh grade and he said, 'Let's see if you can keep it up.' That's what he said."

34. "I think part of why I became a teacher was to be everything he wasn't. And then I stopped being a teacher. So what am I now?"

35. "I had a panic attack in the parking garage at work last month. A full one — shaking, couldn't breathe, the whole thing — and I sat in my car for forty minutes before I could drive."

36. "I've started taking the stairs instead of the elevator because elevators make me anxious now. But then the stairwell makes me anxious too. Mostly I'm just anxious."

37. "Do you ever have a client who you just think — this one's going to take a really long time? I think I might be that person."

38. "I'm not fishing for reassurance. I'm being sincere. I think there's a lot of damage here."

39. "The divorce was two years ago. Shouldn't I be over this by now? People keep suggesting I should be over this."

40. "My mom calls every Sunday and asks if I'm 'getting back out there' and I have to actively resist the urge to hang up."

41. "I've been on two dates since the divorce, both disasters, and now the thought of dating someone new makes me feel genuinely ill."

42. "The second date — she was nice, she was funny — but at dinner I caught myself looking for flaws, like building a case against her preemptively. That's not right, is it?"

43. "I think I trust almost nobody right now. Including myself."

44. "Especially myself, actually. I didn't see it coming with Dana. I thought we were fine. So what does my judgment mean anymore?"

45. "I used to be good at reading people. That was my thing. And now I feel like I was blind my whole life."

46. "Ryan sends me these emails every few months saying he wants to talk. I haven't opened a single one."

47. "I've drafted responses. I've drafted about twelve responses. I never send them."

48. "Some of the drafts are angry. Some are just sad. One of them I read back and it scared me because it was very calm and logical and I don't know what that means."

49. "I'm not going to do anything to Ryan. I want to be clear. I just have a lot of unresolved — I don't know. Grief? Rage? Both?"

50. "The anger comes in waves. Sometimes at Dana, sometimes at Ryan, sometimes at myself, sometimes at nobody specific — just this free-floating fury."

51. "Last week I punched my couch. A throw pillow, technically. And it didn't help at all, which I expected, but I still did it."

52. "I've been eating to feel something. Or eating to feel nothing. I can't tell which one it is, and that probably matters."

53. "I found a photo of the three of us — me, Dana, and Lily at Cedar Point from 2018 — and I stood there holding it for twenty minutes before I could decide what to do with it."

54. "I put it in a shoebox under the bed. Which is probably deeply symbolic of something."

55. "I find it very hard to make decisions now. Small ones, big ones. What to eat, whether to call my mom back, whether my life has a trajectory."

56. "I used to be so decisive. In the classroom, I made a hundred judgment calls a day. Now I stand in the aisle at Walgreens for fifteen minutes choosing shampoo."

57. "Sometimes I wonder if the version of me that was confident and decisive was just performing. And this is the real one."

58. "That thought is one of the scariest ones I have."

59. "I feel guilty about Lily more than I feel almost anything else. That's the dominant feeling."

60. "She deserves a dad who can take her to the park without having to mentally prepare for three days."

61. "I do take her to the park. I want you to know that. When she's here, I show up. But it costs me more than it should."

62. "After she goes back to Dana's on Sunday nights, I usually sit on the floor of her room — the corner I've set up for her — and I don't know. Just sit there."

63. "I bought her a purple rug for that corner. She said purple was her favorite color. That made me feel like I got something right."

64. "She told me last visit that some kids at school were being mean to her and I felt so helpless. So incredibly helpless."

65. "I wanted to fix it and I couldn't and I started imagining all these worst-case scenarios for her whole future and I couldn't stop the spiral."

66. "I have a very vivid imagination and it's working against me constantly right now."

67. "I used to use it to build lesson plans. Now it just generates catastrophic scenarios at 3 in the morning."

68. "I lie awake thinking about money. I'm not broke, but I think about it obsessively — like I'm always one car repair away from disaster."

69. "The divorce cost me a lot. Not to be materialistic. But it did."

70. "I'm very aware that this apartment, this life, is a scaled-down version of the one I planned. And I'm not sure if I'm building toward something or just parked here."

71. "I've been watching a lot of history documentaries at night. Which is either a sign I still love history or a sign I'm hiding in it."

72. "Probably both."

73. "I looked up one of my old students on Instagram last week. She was at college, posting photos with friends, laughing. And I felt proud and devastated at the same time."

74. "I don't want to go back to teaching. I need to be honest about that. I don't think I can hold a classroom together when I can barely hold myself together."

75. "But I don't know what else I am. That job was my identity and I walked away from it and I haven't found anything to replace it with."

76. "The data entry job — I took it because it required nothing of me. And that felt like a relief for the first six months. Now it feels like a punishment."

77. "I've been reading a lot about depression. Self-diagnosing, I know. But I wanted to understand what's happening to me."

78. "I read that thing about how depression lies to you. Tells you it's always been this way. I believe that intellectually. I just can't feel it."

79. "You've given me some good frameworks in these sessions and I do think about them during the week. I just can't always access them when I need them."

80. "The CBT thought journal — I've been doing it. Three days out of seven, which isn't perfect, but it's something."

81. "Some of the entries are very dark. I was going to tear them out before coming today but I thought that was probably bad practice."

82. "Here. You can look at it if you want. Page six."

83. "I wrote that I feel like a building that's structurally sound from the outside but has a rotting foundation. That's the most accurate metaphor I've found so far."

84. "I don't want people to know I'm in therapy. I know that's a stigma thing. I know you're going to gently challenge that."

85. "I grew up in a household where you dealt with things yourself or you didn't deal with them. So sitting in this chair feels like admitting defeat, some days."

86. "Other days it feels like the bravest thing I do all week. Those days are less frequent but they exist."

87. "I've been drinking more. Not alarmingly, I don't think. But I have a beer or two most nights now and I never used to."

88. "I'm aware that's a coping mechanism. I'm not proud of it. I'm just telling you because I think you should know."

89. "I had a moment last week that I keep coming back to. A genuinely good moment. Lily and I were watching a documentary about the Roman Empire and she asked me a question and I just — lit up. For about fifteen minutes, I was completely myself."

90. "And then I thought, 'Where has that been?' and it made me sad again. But also — it's still in there somewhere, right?"

91. "That's the question I carry around with me. Is the old Marcus still in there, or did he die somewhere around 2022?"

92. "I'm scared that therapy won't work. That I'll do everything right and still feel exactly like this at fifty."

93. "I'm scared that I've already been too much of a burden on the people who love me and they're running out of patience."

94. "I don't sleep well before our sessions. I lie awake trying to figure out what's most important to say, like I might waste your time if I pick the wrong thing."

95. "I feel like I owe it to Lily to get better. And then I feel guilty for needing an external reason to get better instead of wanting it for myself."

96. "I don't know if I love myself right now. I think that's an honest thing to say."

97. "I want to be better. I want it genuinely, not just for Lily, but for — the guy who used to love history and run 5Ks and trust people. I want to give him a chance."

98. "I just need someone to tell me this isn't permanent. I know you can't promise that, but I need to hear it anyway."

99. "I'm glad I came today. Even on the days it's hardest to come, I think I'm glad afterward. Does that count for something?"

100. "I'll do the thought journal every day this week. All seven days. I'll try. That's the best I can give you right now — that I'll try."
